info.description:
Use this API as an analysis provider to publish offerings, find eligible Jobs, read their inputs, record execution Attempts, and submit results or failure reports. A Job is a user's analysis request; an Attempt records this provider's execution lifecycle for that Job. Listing a Job does not assign it or grant exclusive access.

### Connect

Use an API-issued provider signing credential and the deployment's canonical HTTPS origin. Public client operations use user credentials and the separate public OpenAPI document. Obtain the enabled contracts, human documentation and signing examples from unsigned `GET /.well-known/api-catalog`: `service-desc` links contracts and `service-doc` links human documentation and signing examples. Catalog anchors identify APIs, not suggested probes. In particular, `POST /provider/v1/hello` changes the published provider advertisement; do not use it solely to test connectivity.

Sign each API request under `x-nmr-request-signature-profile`, with a fresh signature and nonce for each send. Signing examples generate headers locally; they do not send requests. Keep private signing keys secret. For JSON messages, include the `schema_id` required by that operation's request schema; bodyless operations have no JSON document. Check HTTP status, problem type, code, and detail before choosing recovery. Signing again does not determine whether a business operation should be repeated.

### Find and execute work

1. To publish or refresh your directory advertisement, send your complete intended announcement with `POST /provider/v1/hello`. Acceptance records the advertisement and its time, not readiness or computation. Hello does not renew an Attempt.
2. List eligible Jobs with `GET /provider/v1/jobs?analysis_kind_ref=...`. The default view contains open Jobs that select this provider and for which it owns no Attempt. Read the specification with `GET /provider/v1/jobs/{job_ref}/input?analysis_kind_ref=...`. Read linked Upload metadata separately at `GET /provider/v1/jobs/{job_ref}/uploads`; downloading bytes requires a separate capability and store request.
3. Persist your `provider_attempt_key` before `POST /provider/v1/execution-attempts/start`. Persist the returned `execution_attempt_ref` and the `input_fingerprint` from Job-input read before beginning computation. Start records an Attempt; it does not launch a worker or grant exclusivity. Confirm the Attempt is still in progress and reconcile your worker records before starting work.
4. You may report current progress through `PUT /provider/v1/execution-attempts/{execution_attempt_ref}/progress`. Progress is an observation, not a terminal result or an expiry extension. Before reporting completion or failure, persist the exact terminal request. Submit it to `POST /provider/v1/execution-attempts/complete` or `POST /provider/v1/execution-attempts/fail`. Completion stores a provider result; it does not establish scientific validity.

### Recover after a lost response or restart

Read live Attempt inventory with `GET /provider/v1/execution-attempts?state=in_progress`, or read one owned Attempt at `GET /provider/v1/execution-attempts/{execution_attempt_ref}`. API state cannot prove what your worker has already done. Follow each operation's `x-nmr-recovery` and the document-level `x-nmr-attempt-recovery`: preserve the same start identity, do not duplicate computation, and resend the exact retained terminal report when recovering its delivery. Hello and progress replacements have different recovery rules; do not automatically resend an older observation or announcement. Expiry is owned by the server and is not renewed by hello or progress.

get.description:
List Jobs of the requested analysis kind for the authenticated provider, newest first. With has_provider_execution_attempt=false (the default), return open Jobs that currently select this provider and for which it owns no Attempt. With true, return open or closed Jobs for which this provider owns at least one Attempt, even after deselection. Every Attempt state counts; other providers' Attempts do not affect these views. Cancelled Jobs are absent. Listing a Job neither assigns it nor grants exclusive access.

The input_schema_id, input_fingerprint, and input_byte_length fields describe the Job's stored text specification, not its linked Uploads. Use the Job Upload-list operation to read those links.

Start each polling cycle without a cursor. Follow next_cursor to read older Jobs; null means no further page was found at that read. Keep the same provider, analysis kind, and attempt view when using a cursor. Pages reflect current eligibility, not a frozen snapshot. Start again without a cursor to discover newly eligible Jobs; a cursor is not a durable checkpoint.

post.description:
Request a fresh download bearer for one current Upload of this Job. The API independently rechecks the requesting provider's Job access and current Upload membership; an earlier metadata read grants no authority. The provider must currently be selected on an open Job or own an Attempt for this open or closed Job. Cancelled and deleted Jobs are inaccessible. Pending bytes return 409. Success returns the store GET URL, bearer, expiry, byte length, and content hash.

Download with a separate GET to download_url, using the header `Authorization: Bearer <capability>`. Send no request body or query parameters. Omit Content-Length, Content-Type, Content-Encoding, and Range headers, including defaults added by an API client. Downloads return the complete file; partial or resumed reads are not supported. The store uses this bearer, not the provider API request signature. Keep the bearer secret and do not log it. Issuance does not contact the store or check its availability; a download can fail independently. Later Job or membership changes do not revoke an issued bearer before its expiry. The same bearer permits repeated store reads until expiry; a store read does not consume it.

Each request with a fresh signature and nonce is new issuance, not receipt replay. No query parameters or request body are accepted.

x-nmr-attempt-recovery.journal: The minimum durable journal records job_ref, provider_attempt_key, the returned execution_attempt_ref, input_fingerprint, local execution phase, and the exact terminal request identity. Persist the attempt reference and input fingerprint before beginning work. Do not derive attempt keys from process IDs, timestamps, or retry counts.
x-nmr-attempt-recovery.server_lifecycle: The server derives expiry eligibility from started_at under its current maintenance policy and records expiry as a persisted terminal transition. No provider heartbeat, hello, progress update, or cleanup request renews an Attempt. The live inventory contains only in_progress Attempts; exact start replay or point read reveals expired. Exact start replay and exact replay of the current progress observation remain safe after expiry, while new progress, completion, and failure conflict.
x-nmr-attempt-recovery.start: Persist a provider-owned provider_attempt_key before the first start request. Reuse it only for the same job, provider, and canonical start facts; after response loss, retry those same facts.
x-nmr-attempt-recovery.terminal: Persist the exact canonical complete or fail request identity before sending it. Every retry for that attempt and outcome must preserve those terminal facts.

held.message: At its latest update, the provider reported that it had retained an outcome report and paused publication for operator review. Delivery is not confirmed.
held.next_action: Contact the provider operator with the Attempt reference.

reconciling.message: At its latest update, the provider reported that it had retained an outcome report and paused publication while automatically checking the API outcome. Delivery is not confirmed.
reconciling.next_action: Wait for the provider's checks. If this remains unresolved, contact the provider operator with the Attempt reference.

retrying.message: At its latest update, the provider reported that it had retained an outcome report and that automatic retries were pending. Delivery is not confirmed.

x-nmr-request-signature-profile.retry_rule: Every retry requires a fresh signature and fresh nonce.
x-nmr-request-signature-profile.signature_label_rule: Use one arbitrary label shared by Signature-Input and Signature.
x-nmr-request-signature-profile.target_rule: Substitute path parameters verbatim without percent encoding. Raw paths reject percent signs, empty segments, and dot segments. Sign the exact raw path and raw query. @query is '?' plus the raw query and is '?' when the query is empty.
x-nmr-request-signature-profile.transport_and_authority_rule: Use HTTPS. Sign the deployment-supplied canonical authority exactly as @authority: DNS names are lowercase, the default :443 is omitted, and an explicit non-default port is retained. The request Host must canonicalize to that same configured authority.
